title: Arignar Anna and Lal Bahadur Shastri: 'Ethical Majority, Not Arithmetical Majority'
summary: During the 1963 Official Languages Bill debate in the Rajya Sabha, Anna argued that language policy cannot be settled by mere headcounts of Hindi speakers: it demands an ethical majority that respects non-Hindi citizens as equal stakeholders.
keywords: Arignar Anna and Lal Bahadur Shastri: 'Ethical Majority, Not Arithmetical Majority'
full_text:
In May 1963, the Rajya Sabha Chamber in New Delhi was charged with tension as the Official Languages Bill came up for deliberation. Union Home Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri presented the government's stance, arguing that Hindi, being spoken by the single largest linguistic group in India, held an undeniable democratic majority.

Rising from his seat, C.N. Annadurai (affectionately known across the subcontinent as Arignar Anna) commanded the floor with resonant English prose and razor-sharp parliamentary logic.

"The distinguished Home Minister reminds us of numbers," Anna began, his voice calm yet piercing. "He argues that Hindi is the language of the majority. But sir, democracy is not merely a game of counting heads! If democracy were reduced to brute headcounts, why should the tiger be the national animal of India instead of the rat? Why should the graceful peacock be our national bird instead of the ubiquitous crow?"

The entire chamber, including the treasury benches, sat transfixed.

Anna continued: "Sir, what we demand is not an arithmetical majority; what the nation requires is an ethical majority! An arithmetical majority can easily become the tyranny of the many over the few. An ethical majority, on the other hand, pauses, reflects, and ensures that the smallest linguistic group feels equally treasured and respected in this great federal union."

Home Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri smiled warmly, stood up, and conceded that while Anna had framed the argument with unmatched rhetorical beauty, the government would ensure that English continued indefinitely alongside Hindi to guarantee that no non-Hindi citizen was ever disadvantaged.

Anna's distinction between brute arithmetic and moral justice remains one of the finest moments in the annals of Indian parliamentary history.

moral: True democracy protects the dignity of all citizens through moral wisdom, never crushing minority heritage under the weight of sheer numbers.
